title: Weight sync: how long a push takes, by model size and fleet size
design_ref: Larger models: two layouts and the weight sync between them
purpose: Push models of 0.6B to 8B parameters from the trainer's GPU into the rollout fleet over NCCL, with one engine and with two, packed and unpacked, and compare with what the network can carry. Then use the measured rate to price a model of 235B.

checks.description: every size from 0.6B to 8B was pushed into the fleet and the push completed
checks.because: The trainer's GPU holds a bf16 model of the same architecture as the engines. The call is the one the real runs use: the engines receive packed buffers and load them in place.

checks.description: the push time grows with the model's size, roughly in proportion
checks.because: Once the model is bigger than a buffer, the transfer is bandwidth-bound: bytes divided by the rate of the slowest link. The time grows a little faster than the size, for the reason in the next check.

checks.description: the push rate stays between the instance type's baseline and its peak bandwidth, and drops towards the baseline for the largest model
checks.because: The instance type promises 5 Gbit/s sustained and 10 Gbit/s for a burst. A fifteen-second iperf run and a one-second push fit in the burst; a push of 16 GB that is repeated does not, and settles near the baseline.

checks.description: a second engine does not double the push time
checks.because: A broadcast sends each byte once from the trainer into the group, so adding receivers costs far less than sending to each in turn.

checks.description: at this network's rate the design's 10-second push of a 235B model is out of reach by more than an order of magnitude
checks.because: The design says to move weights over the GPU fabric, not the pod network. This cluster has no GPU fabric between nodes, which is why its sync stage looks the way it does in S03.

checks.description: packing does not slow the push: the gap between packed and unpacked is no larger than the spread between repeats
checks.because: Packing cuts the number of NCCL calls. With a few hundred tensors the saving is small next to the time the bytes take on the wire, and the same configuration varies from run to run by about as much as the two variants differ.

checks.description: an engine that spends the whole GPU on its KV budget cannot receive the weights
checks.because: The packed receive buffers are two copies of 1 GiB on the engine's GPU, outside the memory fraction vLLM was told to use. This is why the rollout fleet runs at 70% here and not the 90% the documentation shows for an 80 GB GPU.
